description: Administrator can select Store only as a service-request execution provider.
Store-only definitions can be validated and published through the existing provider registry.
Published versions snapshot the selected store-only mode.
Ticket routing controls are hidden when Store only is selected.
The editor explains that Store only retains the response without creating a ticket.
Existing and newly created definitions default to ticket-only unless explicitly changed.
Store-only submission retains the published definition version and raw answer payload.
Store-only submission retains requester, client, contact, timestamps, and attachments.
Store-only submission reaches a successful terminal execution status with null ticket and workflow ids.
Store-only submission creates no ticket.
Store-only submission emits no ticket notification, ticket-domain event, or workflow execution.
Authorized MSP users can retrieve store-only submissions from definition-scoped history.
Client portal users can retrieve store-only submissions only for their own client account.
History and detail views present store-only success without requiring a ticket link.
A portal form attempt carries a stable opaque client submission key across retries.
Same-key sequential retries return the existing submission without re-executing its provider.
Same-key concurrent retries produce one submission and at most one downstream execution.
Different or absent submission keys preserve distinct-submission and compatibility behavior.
Ticket-only retries create exactly one ticket while retaining the response.
Validation and attachment failures create neither a submission nor downstream side effects.
